newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Macquarie executive charged over TNT.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Macquarie executive charged over TNT.

text.p: Investment bank Macquarie Bank Ltd said on Monday that one of its executives, Simon Hannes, had been charged under the Financial Transaction Reports Act in connection with an investigation into option trading in TNT Ltd.

Hannes had been on extended leave from Macquarie from August 1, 1996, but was available for part time consultation, Macquarie said. Macquarie was the adviser to TNT Ltd on the eventually successful takeover bid for the transport group by Dutch telecommunications and postal group Koninklijke PTT Nederland NV (KPN).
Hannes intended to pleady not guilty, Macquarie said.
Hannes is a senior executive of the bank's corporate advisory division, but was not part of the team working on the TNT transaction, Macquarie said.

"The bank has been informed that the charge has been laid in connection with an investigation into option trading in TNT in September 1996," it said. "Macquarie Bank will co-operate fully with any further investigation by the ASC (Australian Securities Commission) and other authorities."
Macquarie managing director Allan Moss said: "Simon Hannes is a respected executive director of the bank who has been with us since 1985. This is extremely concerning for all of us."
Moss said he could not comment further on matters before the court.
KPN annnounced an agreed A$2.0 billion bid for TNT on October 2 which completely surprised the market.
A man known as Mark Booth made about A$2.0 million in profits from trading in TNT options which had been virtually worthless before KPN's A$2.45 per share cash offer for TNT.
TNT's shares had been trading around A$1.60 at the time. Booth spent about A$90,000 on the options transactions.
Booth has not identified himself or cooperated with authorities, although they have a photograph of him.
The Australian Securities Commission (ASC) won court approval in October last year to freeze the profits made by Booth and two other traders which amounted to more than A$9.0 million.
The ASC said in November it was continuing its investigations of a number of people who traded in options prior to the takeover announcement.
It said TNT and KPN had co-operated with the ASC and had provided the names of over 100 people who participated in the takeover negotiations.
Macquarie's shares were down 35 cents at A$8.40 at 3.00 p.m. (0400 GMT).
